articleTitle: A Least-Squares-based Adaptive PI Controller for grid-tied DC-AC converters
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Renewable energy generation has been a feasible solution for global energy matrix transformation. For this application, grid-tied power converters with LCL filters are commonly used as interfaces between clean energy sources and the electrical grid. However, the LCL filter can cause instability on current loops of fixed-gain controllers due to its resonance peak. Therefore, this work proposes a discrete-time PI (Proportional Integral) Controller, based on Least-Squares algorithm, to mitigate the resonance peak, through active damping, and grid-injected current control. It is highlighted that the proposed method does not need resonant controllers for grid disturbance rejection, and that it is robust to grid impedance uncertainties. Simulation results are presented to corroborate the viability of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: A Least-Square-based RMRAC for Grid-tied Voltage Source Inverters with LCL Filter
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Renewable energy generation systems commonly use LCL filters as interfaces between them and the grid, aiming to reduce the harmonic content of Voltage Source Inverters. However, the LCL filter presents a relevant resonance peak that can lead the closed-loop to instability. Therefore, aiming to mitigate it, and provide an adequate current injection into the grid, in this paper is presented a Least-Squares-based Robust Model Reference Adaptive Controller. The proposed control strategy can track reference currents fast, while rejecting exogenous disturbances without needing additional control loops. Besides, the controller is robust enough to consider the LCL filter as a first order transfer function during its design, which allows it to use a first order reference model, reducing the complexity inherent to adaptive control strategies. Simulation results are presented to discuss the feasibility of a proposed control strategy for grid-injected current control.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Charging Strategy in Smart Grids with Distributed Generation
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper proposes a charging strategy for electric vehicles (EVs) connected in smart grids with distributed generation. The main objective of the proposed strategy is to optimize the charging of EVs during the photovoltaic (PV) generation surplus, considering a performance index where the charging power of EVs in a specific mode is optimized. The proposed strategy employs a particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm to define the optimum power dispatch for EVs connected in the mode with optimization. Different charging modes of EVs are considered, addressing priorities and aspects in the provision of charging power. Simulation results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Smart Early Flood Monitoring System Using IoT
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a significant increase in global demand for near actual facts on natural disasters. Time is vital during a disaster event in order to evacuate vulnerable people at risk, minimize the socio-economical, ecological and cultural impact of the event and restore society to normal as soon as possible. In this project, "Smart Early flood monitoring system using Internet of things (IoT)", an intelligent system is proposed that monitors variety of natural phenomena in order to forecast a flood so that people may prepare for it and limit the damage it causes. The system monitors environmental elements, which include humidity, temperature, water level, water increase rate, and rainfall, to detect a flood. Then the flood prediction is done using IoT enabled sensors data and machine learning with the help of MATLAB. Time Series Forecasting is used in this project to describe an innovative technique to flood prediction. To analyze, the previously acquired runtime data of a given period of time is taken by the prediction model in the form of a dataset and flood risk is anticipated. The project was successfully demonstrated through hardware implementation. When a flood occurred during the testing stage of the product, a flood was successfully detected. Using Wireless Fidelity (WIFI) technology, it can send data to the server as soon as possible. All of the detection alarm systems functioned normally. This system successfully triggered an alarm upon detection. Time Series Forecasting prediction model that assisted in predicting the next few days' flood and rain outcomes, were relatively accurate. Because the device is not overly expensive, the system is adequate and accurate for this critical task.

articleTitle: Design Methodology for the DC Link Current Controller of a Series-Connected Offshore Wind Farm
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The series-connected offshore wind farm is an emerging configuration where the wind energy conversion units are connected in series through the dc terminals of their converters. It allows reaching high-voltage levels without need for an offshore substation with a bulky step-up transformer and a huge rectifier in an offshore substation. On the receiving-side of the dc transmission, in the onshore substation, a modular multilevel converter is used to control the voltage or current of the dc link before injecting the energy supplied by the wind farm into the mains. In this work, it is presented a design methodology to control the dc-link and the three-phase currents of the modular multilevel inverter in the synchronous reference frame. The relation between the dc link and the q-axis currents allows to design an outer control loop and the controllers to regulate the dc link current. Results of digital simulations carried out with PSCAD/EMTDC software are used to validate the proposed system and demonstrate the performance of the controllers.

articleTitle: Inner Loop Controllers for Grid-Forming Converters
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: In this paper, a detailed implementation in discrete-time domain of an inner loop voltage controller with current limmiter for grid-forming converters with LC-filter connected to the grid is presented. A state feedback control law which depends on the states of the converter and of the internal model controller is considered. A resonant controller is also designed for the fundamental frequency of the grid voltage. The stability analysis of the proposed controller is then evaluated with virtual impedance and virtual admittance implementations. Simulation results on a Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) are presented to validate the proposed controller and compare the different virtual impedance implementations.

articleTitle: A Robust Adaptive Predictive Super-Twisting Sliding Mode controller for grid-tied converters
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents a Robust Adaptive Predictive Super-Twisting Sliding Mode controller for grid-injected current control of a grid-tied power converter with LCL filter. The proposed controller is robust enough to consider the LCL filter model as a first order transfer function in its design. Also, the only prior information about a plant is its relative degree and gain’ sign. To implement it, the controller only requires system output measurements. Experimental results are presented to corroborate the controller’s performance.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis among Steinmetz-based analytical models applied to inductors using iron powder material considering DC bias
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: In this work, core loss in inductors with DC bias is analyzed, with different flux densities, frequencies and duty cycles, while comparing Steinmetz-based models (OSE, MSE, IGSE and WSE) to experimental results. The losses estimated on a finite element analysis (FEA) software simulation are included in the comparison. Experimental results indicate the most accurate model according to waveform using iron powder (High Flux) material. As contribution, two main insights are given. The first is that the influence of DC Bias in High Flux material has been found to be negligible, which has not been shown. This means that Steinmetz-based models which do not consider DC Bias may be used to estimate losses in the material. The second insight is in regard to the usage of different Steinmetz-based analytical models. It is demonstrated that the actual Steinmetz coefficients that are used influence the results greatly, much more so than the difference among the models themselves. To demonstrate this fact, it is shown that the original Steinmetz equation, the simplest analytical model, is sufficient to describe core losses, given proper coefficient adjustment.

articleTitle: Four-Switch Five-Level Common-Ground Transformerless Inverter
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents a common-ground five-level transformerless inverter for solar photovoltaic (PV) applications. In the proposed inverter, the grid neutral line is directly connected to the negative pole of the dc bus eliminating the common-mode leakage current which is a critical problem in grid-connected PV systems. Moreover, the proposed inverter has only four power switches, making the first five-level common-ground topology with less than six switches found in the recent literature. In addition to low switch count, only two switches are operating in high-frequency. The operation modes, the design guidelines as well as a modulation strategy are presented. Simulation and experimental results are obtained to demonstrate the performance of the proposed inverter.

articleTitle: Forecasting of photovoltaic power generation using deep learning AI
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The generation of electricity with photovoltaic (PV) panels is one of the alternatives that is currently the most expanding among renewable energy sources. In this scenario, the prediction of PV generation is essential for the safe and reliable operation of energy distribution systems, especially when using smart grids. The present study aims to predict the energy generation of a PV plant through the use of artificial intelligence (AI) with the most up-to-date knowledge in this area. For this, an artificial neural network (ANN) with a Long Short Term Memory layer and ReLU activation function was implemented in Matlab software. This ANN configuration, also known as deep learning (DL), uses an information bank containing data on energy generated at daily intervals. The methodology used in this approach brings a broad update of this theme and made it possible to define the parameters for better functioning of the DL. Finally, it can be concluded that DL results in a more accurate prediction when using a larger database in the network training phase. Thus, this work contributes to better planning of PV generation and to the estimation of energy generation using AI.

articleTitle: Communication Technologies Comparison for Electric Power Quality Monitoring - Fuse Sensor
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The electrical energy quality is affected by factors such as faults and interruptions, and energy concessionaires have been looking for ways to innovate, control and mitigate the causes that affect the electrical energy quality and making the network more reliable. In this way, the concessionaire has implemented the IoT (Internet of Things) concept and the Smart Grid (Smart Electricity Grids) in its energy distribution networks. The modernization of communications networks, provided that the connection of IoT applications were made through LPWAN technologies in the sub GHz bands and FSK modulation that offers low energy consumption and long range in its physical layers. Thus, this article presents, analyzes and compares LPWAN technologies such as LoRa and SigFox and also on FSK technology for coverage tests in some regions in the state of Espírito Santo, Brazil. From the preliminary results obtained taking into account the chosen test sites, it was observed that LoRa technologies presented better results in communication and coverage in relation to SigFox and FSK technologies.

articleTitle: Topologies Analysis of Transformerless PV Inverters with Leakage Current Reduction
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo R. D. R. Da Silva

abstract: Photovoltaic inverters concentrate much of the intelligence and control over the operation of the grid-connected photovoltaic system. The use of transformers in your topology reduces system performance, increases the weight, size and cost of inverters. Thus, the use of transformerless inverters is favored, especially in low power applications, where a low cost, light and efficient system is desired. However, the use of topologies without transformer generates some problems, the main one being the leakage through parasitic capacitances, intrinsically present in photovoltaic modules. High leakage current circulating in the system degrades power quality injected into the electrical grid and causes the activation of protections improperly, putting jeopardize the safety and reliability of the system. In this sense, this work performs an analysis, through simulations in a MATLAB/Simulink environment, of topologies of transformerless single-phase inverters that can deal with leakage current.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Genetic Algorithm Based Optimal Design Methodology for LLC Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents a specific design methodology for the LLC series resonant dc/dc converter employing evolutionary algorithms. Supported by the Pareto frontier, the proposed design procedure defines the resonant tank elements that outcomes in reduced RMS resonant tank current and reduced series resonant tank capacitor RMS voltage. Multi-objective Genetic Algorithm is employed as the optimization tool. The feasibility of the methodology is shown by the design of an LLC dc/dc converter with 400 V input voltage, 100 V output voltage, and 100 W output power. In comparison to the classical design, simulation results show a reduction in up to 26% and 40%, respectively, for resonant tank RMS current and series resonant capacitor peak voltage when the converter is designed by the proposed design procedure. These results highlight the superior performance of the proposed design in comparison to the classical methodology.

articleTitle: Dead-Time Compensation for Grid-Following Inverters with SVM2PC
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents a dead-time compensation method for grid-tied inverters controlled by Space Vector Modulated Model Predictive Control. This method is general and can be applied to grid-tied inverters with an LCL filter and large high-frequency ripple in the inverter-side currents, which can result in multiple zero crossings in the currents during each switching period. A current prediction over the switching sequence is proposed to obtain the current polarity information at each switching transition, allowing to determine the effect of the dead time in the inverter output voltages and compensate the duty-cycles to maintain the original instants of the switching transitions. The constraints obtained from the dead-time compensation method are included in the optimization problem of the control algorithm to ensure operation in the feasible region of the space-vector diagram. In addition, hardware-in-the-loop results are obtained to demonstrate the good performance and effectiveness of the proposed dead-time compensation method.

articleTitle: Development of Practical Extension Activities with High School Students to Encourage entry into Engineering Careers
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The work presented in this article aimed to integrate students from elementary and high school with the reality of the university, taking to school some subjects and activities developed in higher education and finally, develop a practical project with students from schools similar to those developed in the university, in order to generate curiosity in young people, so that they continue studying this area. This project was subdivided into two stages, the first stage (teaching electronics) and the second stage (teaching programming). The electronics teaching stage was subdivided into 5 modules (electrical circuits, analog electronics, digital electronics, electronic instrumentation and programming) and the programming teaching stage was a Python course. With this, it was worked with young people and teenagers, who many times still don't know the profession they want to follow, and this project mapped out the profile of the students and through practical activities, showed the path to be followed for the technology sector. In this way, the goal is to show the students how great this area of study is and to provoke curiosity, so that they become interested in starting their professional life in this segment, which are courses in the technology area.

articleTitle: Dynamic Modeling and Control of the LLC Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Due to the high power density, efficiency and ability to regulate the output voltage over a wide range, the resonant LLC converter has been one of the main choices in power converter designs. One characteristic of this converter is the absence of a constant operating point for the voltages and currents in the resonant tank, which makes it impossible to use mean value modeling techniques, as in pwm converters. In this context, this paper seeks to present the generalized averaging model theory to dynamically model the resonant LLC converter. Furthermore, it is also discussed about the linearization of this model and control aspects of the output voltage. The results show a good ability of the model to characterize the dynamics of the converter.

articleTitle: Multi-Input Split-Source Inverter (MISSI)
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Distributed power generation systems can require the interconection of several and independent energy sources demanding different converter topologies. Recently, a range of impedance source converters has emerged, presenting the capability to provide buck-boost feature in a single conversion stage. The split-source inverter (SSI) has been proposed as a new option among impedance source inverters. This topology requires the same number of active switches of the conventional VSI, three additional diodes and the same eight switching states. This paper proposes the multi-input split-source inverters (MISSI). The proposed topology allows the connection of multiple independent sources, without the need for additional active switches. In addition, it is presented a finite set model predictive control (FS-MPC) strategy for the grid connected operation. An optimal switching state is defined by minimizing a proper cost function through a model that predict the future behaviour of the input and output currents. Simulation results are presented to demonstrate the operation of the proposed topology and controller performance.

articleTitle: Optimized Parameters Initialization of a RMRAC Controller Applied to Grid-Connected Converters
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo J. D. de O. Evald

abstract: This work aims to present a proposal for optimized initialization of parameters with the aid of meta-heuristics of a Robust Model Reference Adaptive Controller (RMRAC). Since adaptive controllers need their initialization of gains and constants for proper tuning of the controller, and this choice of gains is related to the designer’s experience, the use of optimization algorithms to choose a suitable set of parameters for the controller is viable, because in addition to presenting optimized performance for the application, it becomes independent of the designer’s experience in tuning the parameters. For optimal tuning of the RMRAC, a Genetic Algorithm (GA) is used, and the controller is applied to the current regulation of a singlephase power converter connected to the grid with an LCL filter. Simulation results are presented, which shows the effectiveness of the proposal when compared to a RMRAC initialized empirically by an expert designer.

articleTitle: p-q Theory Based Predictive Control for Voltage Regulation and Harmonic Compensation of Standalone SEIG
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper deals with a predictive power control strategy using the Instantaneous Power Theory (p-q theory) for shunt compensation of an distributed off-grid generation system based on a self-excited induction generator (SEIG), ensuring power quality through voltage regulation and harmonic compensation. Furthermore, the controller reference signals are calculated from active and reactive power obtained by the p-q theory, in order to perform an optimized control. The inverter employed is a three-leg voltage source inverter (VSI), which is a well known simple solution for this application. Since the inverter has a finite switching possibilities, a discontinuous control is chosen to predict the next switching state that minimizes the cost function, for that, a FS-MPC strategy is defined. Simulation results are presented in this paper in order to validate the proposed compensation control system based on p-q theory.

articleTitle: Powertrain Requirements and Performance Estimation of Vehicles Converted from Internal Combustion to Electrical Traction
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This work addresses a method for determining the requirements of an electric powertrain applied to an existing car with an internal combustion engine to be converted to electrical traction with minimal mechanical modification. The analysis starts by considering the vehicle’s mechanical coefficients and standard driving cycles FTP 75, NEDC, and NBR 7024. Next, the dynamic model is considered with the car operating under the driving cycles considering that the original gearbox is maintained. As a result, the requirements of the electrical machine in terms of torque and power versus speed are obtained as well as the car performance in terms of acceleration, maximum speed, and hill-climbing capacity. The method is applied to a case study considering a VW-UP!.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control for Common Grounded Photovoltaic Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Transformerless inverters are a compact and high efficiency solution for the grid connected Photovoltaic (PV) systems, however the leakage currents have to be mitigated. Common-Grounded (CG) inverters are an attractive solution for this trouble, once the negative pole of the PV string is directly connected to the neutral terminal, the common voltage is constant and the current is theoretically eliminated. On the other hand, multilevel CG inverters present improved quality of output voltage, however the grid current and the capacitor voltage have to be properly controlled. This paper presents Model Predictive Controllers (MPC) for a CG PV Multilevel Inverter. Two MPC structures are presented: the first that employs a classical multi-objective technique with single cost function and the second is a method that dismiss weighting factors. Simulation results are presented to demonstrate the performance of the presented controllers.

articleTitle: Educational graphic tool for comprehension of relays 50/51, 67 and 21 operation
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The development of softwares, which explore graphic and simple use tools, are efficient for the educational development of students, primarily in areas correlated to engineering, as numbers and graphs are broadly explored. That way, this article aims to develop a tool through the software Excel in order to verify the operation of relays 50/51, 67 and 21, for both impedance and admittance, which are essential to the protection of the electric power system. Through an intuitive user friendly interface, the software is adequate with the available literature and stimulates learning in a simple manner.

articleTitle: Current balancing of scalar-controlled induction motors with imbalanced cables
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Current imbalance can appear when driving induction motors through long imbalanced cables. The imbalance increases motor losses and creates torque ripple and vibrations. So far, modifications to the power equipment, e.g. the cable or the transformer, have been proposed as a solution to the problem. This paper proposes a control method that provides current balancing capability for scalar-controlled variable speed drives. The method is based on the extraction of the negative-sequence current component of the motor currents using Second-Order Generalized Integrators (SOGIs) and its suppression by means of a Synchronous Reference Frame (SRF) current controller. The novelty of the method lies on the fact that the frequency and angle information required by the SOGIs and SRF controller are obtained directly from the scalar algorithm, thus offering a simple, robust and computationally effective implementation. Simulation results in MATLAB/Simulink are presented to illustrate its operating principles and demonstrate its effectiveness.

articleTitle: An IoT-Based Smart Microgrid System For Rural Areas
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Energy is one of the world's most important economic, environmental, and sustainability concerns. To improve living standards and reduce poverty, developing countries, in particular, need reliable, accessible, safe, and effective energy services. In recent years, many solar photovoltaic (PV)-based DC microgrids have been developed to provide electric power to rural areas in developing countries. This research paper has proposed an IoT-based smart microgrid system for rural areas with an advanced control system for the optimal microgrid operation using the internet. The solution is provided by thinking a group of people living in a remote area. This prototype would detect the branch's failure and it could be managed from anywhere at any time with the help of internet. The power ratings would be displayed to the authority via a power monitoring system. In case of an emergency, a generator would be used to provide power to the rural region. The simulation of the projects was successfully done with satisfied results.

articleTitle: A Novel H7 Transformerless Single-Phase Inverter Topology for Leakage Current Reduction
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo R. D. R. Da Silva

abstract: In the case of photovoltaic inverters connected to the electrical grid, a transformer is used for reasons of galvanic isolation and adjustment of the voltage level between the input and output. However, the presence of the transformer causes a reduction in the efficiency of the system and an increase in the volume of the converter. Therefore, there is a trend in the development of transformerless grid-connected inverters. Due to the way PV modules are constructed, an equivalent stray capacitance is formed between the PV cells and their grounded structure during their operation (due to regulatory safety requirements). Without using sophisticated topologies, the lack of galvanic isolation causes some problems, such as common mode voltages and earth leakage currents through the stray capacitances of the modules. Therefore, this article aims to present an analysis of the more traditional topologies of single-phase photovoltaic inverters connected to the electrical grid without a transformer, as well as the proposal of a new topology in PSIM and MATLAB/SIMULINK simulation environment

articleTitle: Evaluation of DLMS/COSEM Data Processing Setups Applied to Smart Metering
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Smart Grids’ growth requires increased energy consumption data from users to ensure the correct grid management. In this way, DLMS/COSEM is a powerful protocol that standards the communication between smart meters and utility central systems, integrating independent device models from different manufacturers. In this paper, we evaluate two communication setups proposing different DLMS/COSEM application layer processing environments, considering locally on a microcontroller connected to the smart meter or externally at a remote data center. In both cases, we present optimization implementations, such as indexing static headers and payload, resulting in reduced data traffic and allowing the use of various wireless communication protocols.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Forces and Mechanical Stresses in Power Transformers: An Analysis Based on Computer Aided Engineering
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This article performs the electromagnetic study of a transformer prototype, through the application of computer simulations with the Finite Element Method using the ANSYS Workbench© software. The study analyses the behavior of electromagnetic forces in transformers, due of the short circuit current, allowing the measurement of radial and axial Lorentz forces at different locations in the windings, and check the mechanical stress suffered. A coupled electromagnetic-structural simulation is performed, where the hoop and compressive stresses are analyzed about the transformer windings.

articleTitle: State Space Predictive Minimum Variance Controller Applied to a Tacho Generator Motor
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This work proposes the project of the State Space Predictive Minimum Variance Controller, this is applied to a Tacho Generator Motor, whose system was assembled and used as a way of evaluating identification, modeling and control techniques. The proposed work is based on the principles of generalized minimum variance control, with a state space approach, in order to analyze the convergence of the system using a state observer with estimated gains with the Observer-Kalman Filter Estimation. In addition to using Reinforcement Learning to tune the control weighting factor of the system.

Author Keywords: State Space Predictive Minimum Variance Controller

articleTitle: Educational Low-Cost Frequency Response Analyzer using Arduino and Software Octave
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Frequency response method is an important approach in the design and analysis of plants and controllers. Bode plot is a simple technique to graphically represent a system frequency response. Getting the Bode plot from experimental data would help students to be motivated and understand the frequency response method, which is usually taught through simulations or theoretical examples. There are tools that allow getting the experimental Bode plot of a plant, but they are expensive. This paper presents an educational low-cost system that experimentally gets the Bode plot using Arduino. The sound card of the notebook intended for programming the Arduino is used to generate the sinusoidal voltages used to get the plant frequency response. A phase detector and two peak detectors allows getting the phase delay and the gain for different frequencies. Those data are sent to the notebook, where a processing program developed in the open-source Octave software used those data to create the Bode plot. Experimental results shows that the proposed hardware can be easily applied as an educational tool to understand frequency response through Bode plot.

articleTitle: Self-Excited Induction Generator Based Generation System Regulation Using Synchronous Generator as Reactive Power Compensator
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This article presents the modeling, simulation and experimental results of a microgrid formed by the parallel operation of the Self-Excited Induction Generator (SEIG) and the Field-wound Synchronous Generator (SG), where the SG acts as a reactive compensator. In the generation system, the SEIG is kept supplying rated power, driven through a primary source of constant power. The SG, on the other hand, is driven by a constant speed source. A Electronic Load Controller (ELC) is used to consume the surplus active power generated by the SEIG that is not used by the consumer unit in order to regulate system’s frequency. When the connected load is greater than the SEIG’s rated power, the SG acts by supplying active power to supply the demand, the ELC is turned off and the frequency control is performed by the speed control of the SG’s primary machine. The reactive power in the microgrid is controlled by the SG static excitation system. This system, based on a Buck converter powered by an external DC source, acts to control the voltage at the Common Connection Point (CCP) of the system by adjusting the SG field voltage. Experimental results shows the performance and reliability of the system against load connections from no-load to rated power.

articleTitle: Virtual Synchronous Generator and Harmonic Suppression Control in a Solid-State Transformer
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The incorporation of distributed generators (DG) to the electrical power system (EPS) has been increasing worldwide. The expectation is that this growth will continue to be observed in coming years due to the popularization of solar photovoltaic energy, which is the most used renewable source in DG. In a scenario of high DG penetration in the EPS, the total rotational inertia of the system would be reduced given that the DG sources are non-inertial, such as, for example, the large synchronous generators (SG) of hydroelectric plants. An alternative to overcome this lack of inertia is to use a control strategy in the inverters at the interface with the EPS such that the EPS perceives the DG system as a SG. This control strategy is called a virtual synchronous generator (VSG). This work aimed to apply a VSG to a solid state transformer (SST) as well as implement and compare two harmonic suppression methods: a linear active disturbance rejection control (LADRC) and an impedance reshaping method, with the purpose of reducing the total harmonic distortion (THD) of the inverter’s output voltage when a nonlinear load is connect to the SST. Real-time digital simulations (RTDS) were carried out with the hardware Typhoon HIL 402 and it was observed that both harmonic suppression methods succeeded in reducing the THD of the output voltage and the VSG control successfully provided virtual inertia to the system.

articleTitle: Signal-Flow Graph Modeling and Control of the DC-DC Multilevel Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper uses a large-signal, small-signal, and steady-state modeling based on the switching flow graph technique for studying the steady-state and dynamic response of the three-level boost dc-dc converter. An additional model includes control loops of the converter in the switching flow graph for over-shoot and settling time requirements. Simulation results confirm adequate voltage regulation.

articleTitle: Study of Back-to-Back Hybrid Filter Applied to a Hot Strip Mill with Cycloconverters
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the back-to-back connection between an active and passive filter in a hot strip mill (HSM) with cycloconverters, in a steel mill located in Vitória Metropolitan Area, ES, Brazil. Through a simulation study, the performance of back-to-back hybrid filter for harmonic compensation and damping of harmonic resonance is evaluated. In addition, the reduction of the effective current in the branches of the passive filtering system is analyzed, in face of a load expansion of the HSM. The obtained results show that the back-to-back filter topology allowed the improvevement of the Power Quality (PQ) and elimination of the overload in the preexisting passive filters with a low rated active filter, when compared to the power system load.

articleTitle: Mathematical models used in photovoltaic system design software: a systematic review and a new proposal
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Currently in photovoltaic generation market, there are many photovoltaic systems simulation software tools that assists the designer in development and validation of photo-voltaic system. Aiming to accompany the growth of photovoltaic generation systems, these tools aim to refine their simulation models and methodologies, including non-linearities and more robust models. However, many tools’ results present generation error negligible for small systems, where 3% at 5% of error margin does not represents impactful loses, but for large power plants, these errors represent thousands of dollars. Faced with this problem, this paper proposes a revision in software tools methodologies most used currently in market: PVsyst and PVsol. Furthermore, this work proposes possible improvements in mathematical simulation models, showing the impacts of temperature mismatch in systems of different ports. The work shows that using a PV system with 4 strings of 10 modules, with a temperature gradient mean about 8ºC, the temperature mismatch has an average impact of 2.3% in generation power loss. Faced with this problem, this paper proposes a revision in software methodologies most used currently in market: PVsyst and PVsol. Furthermore, paper proposes possible improvements in mathematical simulation models, showing the impacts of temperature mismatch in systems of different ports.

articleTitle: Four-phase Buck Converter Design and Thermal Modeling Using FEA Simulation
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Equipment with high efficiency, high power density, reduced size and low cost are in demand in the automotive industry. This work presents a method to design and model a high power-density four-phase DC-DC Buck converter for an automotive application and using the components operating temperature as a design criteria. A parameter sweep is done to select the operating point of the DC-DC converter combined with an iterative method to select part numbers, where preference is given to components that are AEC-Qxxx qualified. The converter is modeled and power losses are computed in SPICE considering the parasitic elements present in the PCB and the dynamic characteristics and non-idealities of the electronic components; thermal modeling is performed using Ansys Icepak. The results indicate that the design meets all electrical and thermal requirements for an automotive application. An efficiency of 95.97% is obtained in a four-phase DC-DC Buck converter that supplies a total of 800 W to 4 loads, in a space of 43.77 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, that is, an estimated power density of 18.28 W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Comparison between methods for the calculation of the electrical potential distribution in the surface of grounded grids
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The analysis of the potentials generated in the ground by the injection of current caused by the grounded networks, whether SWER or three-phase two-wire system, is essential to study the establishment of the maximum step voltages that emerge in these systems, and, thus, guarantee the safety of everyone who is close to these network structures. Thus, it is necessary to develop a robust calculation methodology which guarantees a good analysis for different grounding configurations, regardless of the level of injected current, the soil resistivity and the thickness of its layers, in order to ensure the best choice in the project of a network grounding that involves direct energizing of the ground. This paper does the comparison between three surface electrical potentials calculation methods using simulations in MATLAB, in order to define which one is the safest method.

articleTitle: Study About Architecture Classification of Bidirectional Non-Isolated Power Converters
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: In this paper an evaluation of the architecture classification of bidirectional power converters is done taking into account the low voltage DC bus as input and high voltage as output. The classification can be input/output as series or parallel, where the series characteristic is the voltage division between the converters, while the parallel characteristic presents the current division feature. Also, in this paper is proposed a new architecture, which present both characteristic of parallel and series approach. To demonstrate the experimental efficiency results of the architectures, six prototypes were built in the laboratory. Efficiency curves was extract from 500 W to 1 kW, where the proposed architecture presented one of the best general efficiency.

articleTitle: Automation of the Tower Allocation Process of an Electric Power Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: In this paper, a program capable of performing the automatic allocation of towers of an electrical energy transmission system, given a topographic profile, is presented. The code utilizes a GENETIC ALGORITHM (GA) as an optimization tool within the MATLAB software. Three genetic operators are used to obtain individuals: Reproduction, Crossover and Mutation. The fitness function evaluates the data related to the components and restrictions of the TRANSMISSION LINE (TL) to estimate the total cost that will serve as a selection parameter when applied in the GA.

articleTitle: A Control Strategy and Cell Balancing Speed Analysis Considering the Integrated Circuit LTC3300-1
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Maria de Fátima N. C. Rosolem

abstract: One of the most important tasks for a Battery Management System (BMS) is the charge distribution among the cells in the battery, a process called cell balancing. This process can be done by two types of circuits, dissipative and non-dissipative, the second one uses intermediary components such as DC-DC converters to move energy among the lithium-ion battery (LiB) cells. As most of the works mainly focus on the theoretical circuits, without considering the available commercial solutions, in this work the non-dissipative circuit based on the Flyback bidirectional DC-DC converter, LTC3300-1 from Analog Devices, is employed to balance a LiB. Then, a cell balancing strategy was developed and used to carry out a study, through numerical simulations, to obtain the IC cell balancing speed according to the number of stacked ICs and the cell balancing current. The results showed that, when the cell balancing current is constant, the cell balancing speed depends on the physical position of the cells to be balanced. Also, an increase in the balancing current means an increase at the same rate in the cell balancing speed. Finally, it was shown that the number of stacked ICs plays a fundamental role in the cell balancing speed.

articleTitle: Evaluation of leakage current in different inverter structures applied in non-isolated power optimizers
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This article presents the design of a power optimizer, composed of five PV modules and five non-isolated Boost DC-DC converters connected in series, in order to obtain the necessary voltage for the DC bus of the central inverter. In the CC-AC stage, three topologies are compared: half-bridge, full-bridge and NPC, in order to analyze the leakage current levels. In addition, with the objective of obtaining greater energy processing, the perturb and observe (P&O) algorithm was implemented in each optimizer, being then evaluated, considering ideal conditions and with partial shading (irradiance variation).

articleTitle: Passive balancing of second life lithium-ion cell by outlier detection for energy optimization
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The use of lithium-ion cells in electric vehicles has a time and mileage established by the manufacturer, when the use period becomes near 8 years or 160k kilometers is said that the battery arrives at the end of the first life. At this point, the battery still has about 80% of its nominal capacity, which becomes viable for a second, less demanding application. Battery cells need a balancing system to minimize potential problems caused by battery imbalance. In this work, a methodology for passive balancing of lithium-ion cells in a second life application is proposed.

articleTitle: Power losses estimation in a GaN-based synchronous Buck LED driver
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents the theoretical and experimental power losses analysis of a Gallium Nitride (GaN)-based Synchronous Buck converter, which employs two enhancement mode (e-GaN) transistors in a half-bridge configuration. This topology is used as the Power Control (PC) stage of a two-stage LED driver. A theoretical method for power loss estimation and distribution is presented. An 180W converter is built and tested experimentally to validate the proposed methodology. Practical efficiency reaches 97%, and the percentage error between the estimated and the experimental efficiency is 0.064%. The efficiency curve, from 10% to 100% of the nominal load is also presented.

articleTitle: Explanatory Review about Rapid Shutdown Systems and Standards to Increase Safety in Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) systems have been extensively used to provide clean energy from small-size solar roof applications to large-size power systems. Although its static conversion-based technology reduces most safety problems related to fatigue, there still some risks inherent to technology. One of these risks are parallel arc faults on dc side that generally occur due to poor installation of external source of fire. During daylight times, these faults cannot be extinct switching off ac circuit breakers since the sun continuously feed the arc by dc side. So, these faults bring high risks for people who live in buildings with PV systems, as well as for firefighters trying to extinguish them. Due this, in last years have been proposed many solutions to mitigate this problem, in special the rapid shutdowns systems. This paper presents an explanatory review of standards, technical data, and papers related to rapid shutdowns systems for PV applications. It is presented of the main existing solutions that can considered for further development of Brazil regulation.

articleTitle: Development of a Three-Phase Converter with Power Derating for Second-Life Battery Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents contributions related to the power distribution and control of second-life batteries in energy storage systems. In this case, Power Electronics plays a major role to perform the interface between the charge and the energy storage stages. In three-phase systems, a zero-sequence component shifts the excess power from one of the converter phases to the others. However, the zero-sequence component increases as the parameter differences among the batteries become more severe. This effect can be mitigated in a delta-connected energy storage system, by controlling the converter reference power. A seven-level cascaded H-bridge converter is proposed for a second-life battery energy storage system and simulation results are presented to confirm the viability of the proposals listed in this work.

articleTitle: Power System Stabilizer Applied to VSG-Based Power Flow Control of DG Systems in Low-Voltage Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents a power system stabilizer (PSS) technique to improve the dynamic performance of power flow control based on the virtual synchronous generator (VSG) approach for distributed generation (DG) systems connected to low voltage networks. The PSS structure is defined based on the dynamic model of the system’s power flow. The PSS technique performance is evaluated through simulation results addressing the grid-connected DG system’s operation with different grid impedance parameters. The results obtained reveal the effectiveness of the theoretical analysis and the proposed control structure.

articleTitle: Dynamic Simulation and Analysis of a Wind Farm Connected to a Transmission Substation
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The power injection of double fed induction generatos machines can affect the energy generation of wind farms interconnected to the power system. In this paper, simulations were made to understand the operation of such machines. These simulations are based on the resolution of the power flow to obtain the initial point of operation and, through the use of differential equations that describe the DFIG–Double Fed Induction Generator, its controls acting on the electrical network. Six DFIG machines were simulated, interconnected to an electric power substation. For this work, it performed the simulations using the MATLAB/Simulink software. Good results were obtained from the DFIG acting through the control of active and reactive power, until the machine stabilizes again, when a sudden voltage variation occurs in the substation. The results showed that the controllers acted to maintain the desired power levels after the voltage variation.

articleTitle: Simulation and Dynamic Analysis of a Wind Farm in the Occurrence of a Fault in the Grid
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The electrical power system is subject to disturbances that affect the balance and dynamics of its operation. Electrical faults are one of the critical causes of these disorders. The study of double-fed induction wind turbines (DFIGs) in short-circuit situation in the system is necessary to understand their behavior at this critical moment and their contribution to the fault current. In this work, 6 DFIGs are simulated with different operating configurations and location in the network in a fault duration of 0.02 s. The simulations showed that the wind turbines vary their behavior according to the operating characteristics, and may interfere with other machines, depending on the arrangement in the system.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of Low-Voltage Ride-Through on the VSG-Based Power Flow Control Applied to Grid-forming DG Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper presents a case study to evaluate the impact of the low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) on the virtual synchronous generator (VSG) strategy performance applied to power flow control in grid-forming distributed generation (DG) systems. For this purpose, the DG system was subject to asymmetrical faults applied to the point of common coupling (PCC) to characterize the LVRT condition. The VSG strategy performance is evaluated through simulation results addressing the grid-connected DG system operation with different scenarios of asymmetrical voltage sags. The analysis presents the main impacts on the system control variables, which can guide the improvement of standard VSG strategies to minimize the impacts caused on the DG power flow control.

articleTitle: Optimal Power Factor Correction and Overvoltage Mitigation in Distributed Generation Unit
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This paper proposes an energy management system (EMS) for a distributed generation (DG) unit based on particle swarm optimization (PSO). The main goal of the proposed EMS is to optimize the profit of the dispatch while maintaining the power factor (PF) and voltage of the connection bus within allowable limits. The EMS considers a cost function composed of two terms. The first term accounts for the economic dispatch, while the second relates to overvoltage mitigation. Moreover, the EMS treats the active and reactive power differently for overvoltage mitigation. At a first attempt, the EMS only uses reactive power to correct the voltage. If this strategy is not enough, the EMS limits the active power generated. The EMS evaluation considers a radial distribution system model and real data of electrical load and irradiance. Simulation results are shown and discussed.

articleTitle: LQI Control applied to a DC-DC Boost Converter in a Standalone PV System
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Standalone photovoltaic (PV) systems without some energy storage element are widely used in rural areas. In this type of systems, the output voltage must be regulated to be at a fixed value, independent of changes in weather conditions or variations in the output load. Therefore, this article presents a Linear Quadratic Integral (LQI) control applied to a DC-DC boost converter in order to regulate the output voltage in an standalone PV system, reducing the impact of external factors. Also, the mathematical modeling of the boost converter used is introduced in this work. The LQI controller design was developed from the previous modeling, using the values of the power circuit. Finally, the proposal is validated by simulations and experimental results obtained through the developed prototype. For this, different tests were performed, changing the irradiation values in the PV panel, changing the DC load at the output of the converter and inserting shading on the PV panel.

articleTitle: Management of Distributed Energy Resources in a Rural Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Microgrids have several elements, such as intermittent distributed energy resources, which bring challenges to the system. In order to overcome these challenges, it is necessary to implement a microgrid controller capable of managing energy resources. This management can keep the system stable. In this study, the management of a rural microgrid is proposed. It contains loads, batteries, energy storage systems, and the following generators: wind, photovoltaic, and diesel. The control strategy reduced costs and ensured energy availability, providing flexibility and security for the grid.

articleTitle: Analysis of technical losses considering charging stations and PV systems
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Currently, the pursuit for more sustainable technologies resulted in a higher emphasis on environmental friendly policies elaboration by institutions. Among these, Distributed Generation (DG), primarily by photovoltaic generation, and the insertion of Electric Vehicles (EVs) in the vehicle fleet are highlighted, although, for the implementation of the latter, charging infrastructure needs to be well consolidated. However, in both cases, it is necessary to conduct studies about their possible impacts in the grid in order to deploy them as efficiently as possible. Therefore, this paper presents an analysis of technical losses (TLs) related to the implementation of charging stations (CS) and photovoltaic distributed generation (PVDG) in order to demonstrate the possible dynamics that these elements introduce into the grid. The analyses are done through the software OpenDSS and reports how each of these technologies impacts the grid in relation to the power demanded from the substation and in the system’s technical losses.

articleTitle: Power Electronics Laboratory Projects Enhance Interdisciplinary Engineering Education
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Delivering modern and interdisciplinary education that provides students with a wide set of engineering skills is essential for addressing the current needs of multiple industrial sectors. With this aim, three power electronics laboratory group projects for higher education students are presented in this paper. The projects focus on i) the development of an Intelligent Power Module-based inverter, ii) the development of a measurement board and iii) their integration with a rapid control prototyping platform. The intended learning outcomes are presented together with the work methodology for each project. Furthermore, it is highlighted that although the projects are discrete in nature, they can be combined to form a complete power converter system which can serve as a platform for further experimentation and research into modern applications, such as renewable energy sources integration and motor drives. The latter is demonstrated through the description and results of tests rigs built using the developed hardware components.

articleTitle: Development of a network of charging stations with franchising application through business model Canvas
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: This article aims to present the development of a startup franchise of charging stations. The focus of this study is to analyse the entrepreneurial functionality through the Business Model Canvas. In between the analysis made for this network, the choice of the charging modes, the sociodemographical analysis of candidate locations for the best employment, analysis of a credit system based in vehicle-to-everything (V2X) technology to develop a new dynamic in the national charging stations market are highlighted. By these means, the possibility of a higher range of interactions with the consumer can be analysed through state of art technology and your possible expansion through a franchising system aiming to catalyse the engagement with these technologies in Brazilian society. Therefore, the article aims to validate the methodology proposed while creating options to develop the national electromobility market according to current national conditions. In conclusion, a viable business model can be created following national policies and sociodemographic situation following the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Design aspects of the electric propulsion of Brazilian Army Leopard vehicles with fuel cells
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: João Olavo da Silva Viana Leite

abstract: This work presents some aspects and challenges of using hydrogen fuel cells to drive armored military vehicles. For this, it is important to consider the advantages and limitations of switching from the combustion engine to electric motors in combat vehicles. In this article, the Leopard 1 A5 BR vehicle of the Brazilian Army is being focused on as an example. This text deals with the main aspects of this conversion related to performance, weight, space, noise, detectable temperature, regenerative braking and autonomy.

articleTitle: Microgrid for electric vehicle fast-charging: an energetic approach to highway operation in the South of Brazil
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: The replacement of traditional vehicles with electric vehicles has been widespread in developed countries, and should continue to grow globally. The development of electric mobility is one of the important steps to achieve a future with zero emission vehicles (ZEV). Battery Electric Vehicles (BEV) do not emit polluting gases, but the guarantee of non-pollution is only achieved when the energy that feeds these vehicles comes from clean sources. Thus, this article is proposed a methodology to estimate the energy self-sufficiency percentage of a microgrid aimed at offering fast recharges to BEV on highways. The plants, wind and photovoltaic, present in the microgrid, have their average monthly generation estimated via simulations in Homer software; and the occurrences of recharges in the microgrid are estimated according to the vehicle flow on the highway and growth of the participation of BEV over time. In the case study, high rates of microgrid self-sufficiency were initially verified, being able to carry out up to 175 recharges of 40kWh per month. As the fleet of BEV grows, this percentage is reduced, yet it remains an important ally to ensure supply from clean sources.

articleTitle: Analysis of the impact of photovoltaic systems on the power factor
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)
abstract: Due to the increase in demand for electricity and the high costs associated with it, final consumers are increasingly interested in generating their own energy. As a result, there has been a significant growth in interest in photovoltaic generators directly connected to the load. However, despite the benefits, such as diversification of the energy matrix and reduction of losses in the distribution network, photovoltaic generators can bring problems related to power quality. In this context, the present article shows the negative impacts that photovoltaic systems have in the power factor (PF) in relation to the tariff group B. It is also shown that both group A and group B consumers change the power factor of the system. The analysis of the negative impacts are made considering a test network, the IEEE 34 bus feeder through the simulation software OpenDSS (Open Distribution System Simulator). In view of the above, the impact on the distribution network is analyzed in relation to the regulations and methods to solve the impacts caused.

articleTitle: Proposal of Prototype of PMU Based on Dynamic Phasors
publicationTitle: 2022 14th Seminar on Power Electronics and Control (SEPOC)

authors.preferredName: Paulo R. D. R. da Silva

abstract: Monitoring systems act decisively in any process, thus maintaining the maintenance and operability of equipment. In this context, the equipment that has been gaining market share by providing synchronized system magnitudes is the Synchronized Phase Measurement Unit(PMU). This equipment is capable of providing the system operator with phasor values of voltages and currents synchronized with a satellite signal. The main objective of this work is to develop, test and validate a PMU, comprising a hardware and software platform for use in research environments.
